name: Yao Hsiao Tung
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Yao Hsiao Tung is the executive chairman and CEO of Hi-P International, which the former DuPont executive acquired as a small tool maker in 1983.
Today it is one of Singapore's largest contract manufacturers of smartphones, tablet computers and consumer electronics with customers such as Apple.
In 2017, he acquired the stake of longtime partner Molex, a manufacturer of electrical connectors owned by U.S. billionaire Charles Koch.
He delisted the company from the Singapore Stock Exchange at a valuation of $1.2 billion in 2021, with the aim of securing greater flexibility in running the business. He plans to relist it by 2030.
In 2024, Temasek-backed 65 Equity Partners invested S$100 million ($74 million) in the company.
forbes_facts: Yao was born in mainland China but moved to Taiwan as a child; he's now a Singaporean citizen.

name: Li Haizhou
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Li Haizhou is chairman of Shenzhen Zhaowei Machinery & Electronics, which he founded in 2001.
The company specializes in designing, developing and manufacturing precision transmission systems.
Its main products include components that are used in automotive, smart home devices, medical technology, robotics and telecommunications.
His wife Xie Yanling is vice chairman of the listed company.

name: Philip Day
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2017-2018); Hurun Global (2018-2023); Sunday Times Rich List (2020); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: One of Britain's wealthiest high street fashion moguls, Philip Day owns Edinburgh Woollen Mill and several other UK fashion brands.
He decided to skip college in order to start working for a British clothing manufacturer and joined Edinburgh Woolen Mill in 2001.
A year later he bought the company outright; it was barely turning a profit.
Day turned it around, acquired other struggling retailers and expanded the company to greater heights.
In 2012 he bought Peacocks, one of the UK's largest fashion retailers, and has worked diligently to revamp its business.
forbes_facts: A keen outdoorsman, Day owns The Scottish Deer Centre, a 55-acre wildlife sanctuary home to more than 14 species of deer that encourages environmental research.
Day previously sat on the board of his local soccer club, Carlisle United, despite reportedly not enjoying the sport.

name: Mario Moretti Polegato
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2006-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Mario Moretti Polegato founded his comfort-focused shoe brand Geox in 1995 with his patented "breathable shoe technology."
Polegato worked at his family's wine business where he got itchy feet, but it was a hot trip to Nevada that inspired him to slice holes in his shoes.
He took his technology to Nike and other footwear giants, who were uninterested; he started his own company instead.
He took Geox public in 2004 while also running the family wine label, Villa Sandi.
forbes_facts: Polegato was named a Knight of the National Order of Romania in 2000, and was appointed Cavaliere del Lavoro, one of Italy's highest civilian honors, in 2005.
He developed his breathable shoe prototype in the mid-1990s with researchers at the University of Padua, a university established in 1222.

name: Laura Diehl
forbes_bio: Laura Diehl is one of the key shareholders of the Diehl Group, representing the fourth generation of the Diehl dynasty.
The Nuremberg, Germany, based family enterprise is a global technology leader, generating annual sales of more than $5 billion.
The group's diversified portfolio includes strategic sectors such as Metall, Controls, Defence, Aviation, and Hydrometering.
The Diehl Group employs a workforce of more than 18,000 people across its various international divisions.
Originally founded in 1902 as a specialised foundry, the company has evolved over four generations into a major international industrial group.

name: Ronald Perelman
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Ronald Perelman is a dealmaker who built a fortune with a diverse array of holdings, from candy to cosmetics.
Perelman sold assets worth billions of dollars to pay off debt in late 2020 after the Covid-19 pandemic ravaged his businesses.
He was a longtime shareholder of cosmetics giant Revlon but lost his holdings during its 2023 bankruptcy proceedings. His daughter Debra was the firm's CEO from 2018 to 2023.
Perelman learned about business from his father. He attended board meetings with him while in elementary school.
He is a prolific art collector who has sold off much of his collection in recent years.
forbes_facts: Perelman's foundation pledged $65 million to Princeton in 2018 but did not follow through, prompting the school to remove his name in 2021 from a new dorm.
Perelman has eight children from five wives.

name: Zhaoxi Lu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2018-2022); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Hurun China (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Lu Zhaoxi, also known as Jonathan Lu, has held numerous posts in the Alibaba Group over the years, most recently vice chairman.
His fortune arises from holdings in Ant Group, the financial services arm of Alibaba Group.
On November 3, 2020, Chinese authorities held up Ant's planned dual IPO listing in Shanghai and Hong Kong due to regulatory concerns.
He holds a graduate certificate in hotel management from Guangzhou University and an MBA from China Europe International Business School.

name: Lin Chang Su-O
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2019-2025)
forbes_bio: Lin is the widow of real estate mogul Lin Rong San. She resigned as chairman of the family's property developer Union Enterprise Construction in 2021.
Lin Rong San died in 2015 and left a $4.2 billion fortune built on real estate developments and investments in northern Taiwan.
Eldest son Jeff Lin runs the publicly traded Union Bank of Taiwan, which was started by his father.
Second son Andy Lin runs the group's media outlets, including Chinese-language newspaper Liberty Times and its sister English-language Taipei Times.
Youngest son Kevin works with another family-owned developer, RSL, which builds upscale residential projects and operates hotels.
forbes_facts: Lin Chang Su-O also chairs her late husband's Lin Rong San Foundation of Culture and Social Welfare.
In 2018 the Lins ended Marriott's franchise agreement for its Taipei hotel to protest the chain's caving in to Chinese pressure by listing Taiwan as part of China.

name: Yu Qibing
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2011-2026)
forbes_bio: Yu Qibing is a former chairman of the Kibing Group, a glass manufacturer.
Zhuzhou Kibing Group listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2011.
The Group is headquartered in Shenzhen, China.
